label: Quantum Cohomology
notes: Chapter 11 spans printed pages 417 through 486 and asks how Gromov-Witten counts deform ordinary cup product into a ring that remembers holomorphic spheres. We travel from three-point invariants through the quantum product, WDVV associativity, the Novikov ring, the projective space example, and the Frobenius-manifold packaging that closes the chapter.

label: From Cup Product to Quantum Product
notes: Ordinary cohomology multiplies cocycles by intersecting the Poincare duals of their cycles. The quantum product adds correction terms that count rational curves passing through three cycles. Each correction carries a formal Novikov variable tracking the curve class, so the classical intersection answer survives intact as the leading term when those variables vanish.

label: Three-Point Gromov-Witten Invariants
notes: The structure constants of the quantum product are the genus-zero three-point Gromov-Witten invariants. They count J-holomorphic spheres in a fixed homology class meeting three cycles dual to the inserted classes. A dimension count over the moduli space forces a degree constraint that pins down exactly which classes and curve classes contribute.

label: The Novikov Ring
notes: Infinitely many curve classes can contribute, so we book-keep them in the Novikov ring of formal series in variables q raised to homology classes. The finiteness condition controlling how many classes appear below each energy level makes products well defined, and setting q to zero recovers ordinary cohomology cleanly as the degree-zero piece.

label: The Small Quantum Product
notes: The small quantum product uses only three-point invariants and lands in cohomology tensored with the Novikov ring. The fundamental class stays a two-sided unit, the product respects a shifted grading coming from the Chern number of the curve class, and the degree-zero curve class reproduces the classical cup product exactly.

label: Associativity and WDVV
notes: The deepest property of the quantum product is associativity. It is equivalent to the Witten-Dijkgraaf-Verlinde-Verlinde equations, a nonlinear system of partial differential equations on the Gromov-Witten potential. Associativity is far from obvious because each product mixes infinitely many curve-class corrections together, so the identity genuinely interlocks those counts.

label: WDVV from the Boundary of M_0,4
notes: Associativity comes from the moduli space of four-pointed genus-zero curves, a sphere whose two special boundary points are nodal configurations. The four marked points split across the node in two distinct ways, and the gluing axiom equates the two boundary classes, producing exactly the WDVV identity and hence associativity of the quantum product.

label: The Gromov-Witten Potential
notes: Packaging all genus-zero invariants into one generating function gives the Gromov-Witten potential. Its third partial derivatives in the cohomology coordinates are precisely the quantum structure constants, so the WDVV constraint becomes a clean differential equation on this single potential function, directly foreshadowing the Frobenius-manifold viewpoint developed at the end of the chapter.

label: Quantum Cohomology of CP^n
notes: The cleanest example is complex projective space. Classically the hyperplane class x satisfies x to the n plus one equals zero. Quantum corrections deform this single relation to x to the n plus one equals q, and that one change generates the entire quantum ring, turning the nilpotent classical algebra into a far richer deformed structure.

label: The CP^1 Multiplication Table
notes: For the projective line the whole ring fits in a tiny table. The only nonclassical entry is H times H equals q, replacing the classical nilpotent relation H squared equals zero. Setting q to zero recovers the classical table, while for positive q multiplication by H becomes semisimple with eigenvalues plus and minus square root of q.

label: Frobenius Structure and Seidel Units
notes: The Poincare pairing, the quantum product, and the potential together form a Frobenius manifold in which the product is symmetric against the metric. Seidel's representation sends Hamiltonian loops to invertible quantum cohomology classes, and in the projective line model the inverse of H is simply H over q, since H times H over q equals one.

label: Synthesis
notes: Quantum cohomology threads three-point invariants into a ring through the Novikov bookkeeping, earns associativity from the boundary geometry of the four-pointed moduli space, computes cleanly for projective space via the relation deforming to q, and reorganizes into a Frobenius manifold whose potential encodes every genus-zero count in one single object.
